correctness.rationale: From F/(1-F)=x(x+c)/(P+dx), direct differentiation gives H=1-(cd-P)x/((x+c)(P+dx)), with derivative sign controlled exactly by cP-dx^2. The unique minimum is m=sqrt(cP/d), its depth is 2sqrt(P)/(sqrt(P)+sqrt(cd)), and F(z)=1/2 iff z(z+c)=P+dz. Solving those three constraints reconstructs c,d,P. Since cd>P, the quadratic for a,b has two positive distinct roots straddling c; w=(c-a)/(b-a) is interior and unique. This proves surjectivity, injectivity and insufficiency of every diagnostic pair. Standalone CHECK.py passed 22503 assertions including independently selected triples; finite checks are only corroboration.

value.rationale: A shallow Hill slope is experimentally ambiguous between heterogeneous independent classes and molecular cooperativity. This theorem determines exactly what three intrinsic, interpretable statistics suffice to calibrate the canonical two-class heterogeneity model, establishes the entire feasible-statistics region and gives an explicit inverse. It is a complete natural identifiability problem rather than a parameter-specific numerical exercise; its limits about noisy measurements and alternative mechanisms are stated.
